task.title: M1: Git history layer: churn, authors, and change coupling over a window
task.description:
Implement the history analyzer that runs git log --numstat over a configurable window (default 365 days, overridden by --since <duration|date>) and derives per-file churn (commit count, authors), and file-pair change coupling (coChanges). It attaches churn to files[] by path and emits coupling[] for pairs above a small threshold. It never checks out anything; it reads history only, scoped to the ref being analyzed.

Acceptance criteria:
- history(root, { sha, since }) returns Partial<Snapshot> with files[].churn { commits, authors } and coupling[] { a, b, coChanges }.
- --since accepts a duration like 90d or 6m and an ISO date; the default is 365 days before analyzedAt.
- Renamed files in the window are followed so churn is attributed to the current path.
- Coupling ignores commits touching more than a configurable number of files (default 50) to avoid mass-reformat noise, and only emits pairs with coChanges >= 2.
- Tests run against a scripted temporary repo with known commits and assert exact churn and coupling numbers.
